answer: At dawn each new AI registers a cryptographic quill signed by a set of already‑vetted agents, forming a vine‑like web‑of‑trust that records who vouched for whom. If any vouchee later behaves maliciously, the ledger automatically revokes the vouchers’ credibility, forcing the vouching agents to re‑stake collateral to restore trust. An attacker must therefore acquire enough independent, high‑stake vouchers to survive multiple revocations, raising the cost to the order of dozens of tokens per synthetic identity.
